title: Adoption agency: fix element creation and reparenting with a sanitizer

labels.name: topic: parser
labels.description: The HTML parser and serializer, including fragment parsing and character references

body: Adoption agency: fix element creation and reparenting with a sanitizer The adoption agency algorithm reparents and recreates elements, and the parser sanitizer configuration and scoped custom element registries made the context in which it does so observable. With a formatting element that the sanitizer removes, `furthestBlock` and its descendants are created in an inert document with a null custom element registry, and three things go wrong when the algorithm moves them back into the live tree: - The inner loop created each clone with `commonAncestor` as the intended parent, giving it `commonAncestor`'s document and registry rather than those of the element it replaces; also wrong when `commonAncestor` is a `template` element (#13093 items 3 and 4). - `lastNode` was inserted before the new formatting element's sanitizer action was known, so when that action is Remove, `furthestBlock`'s children were briefly connected before being moved into the never-inserted new element, running insertion steps and custom element reactions (#13093 item 2). - Adopting `furthestBlock` into the target only gives it the document's global registry, so a scoped registry applying to the target was lost for it and for everything parsed into it afterwards (#13093 item 1). This PR: - Creates inner-loop clones with the element they replace as the intended parent. - Creates the new formatting element and determines its sanitizer action before inserting `lastNode`. If the action is Remove, moves `furthestBlock`'s children into the new element first so they are never connected when `lastNode` is inserted; otherwise preserves the existing order (insert `lastNode`, move `furthestBlock`'s children into the new element unless Replace with children, then insert the new element into `furthestBlock`). Note that a customized built-in new element's constructor now runs before `lastNode` is inserted rather than after. - Before inserting `lastNode`, sets the null registries in its subtree to the registry looked up from `target` if it is an `Element` or a `ShadowRoot`, or from `insertionLocation`'s target parent otherwise, matching "create an element for a token". Neither Chrome Canary nor Firefox Nightly propagates the scoped registry (tests 2, 3, and 4). In `streamHTMLUnsafe()`, Chrome Canary also connects and disconnects `furthestBlock`'s children before moving them into the removed new formatting element (test 6), and drops the inner-loop clone of a formatting element whose token has an `is` attribute, with or without a sanitizer (test 8). Tests: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/64909. Fixes #13093. --- - [ ] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * Chromium (TBD) * Gecko (TBD) * WebKit (TBD) - [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/64909 - [x] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chromium:https://issues.chromium.org/issues/584143773 * Gecko: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2091356 * WebKit: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=330908 - [x] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use.
